title: Prune the redundant TensorView axis mapping surface
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: TensorView already retains axes as one validated, unique, canonical immutable tuple, while the axis_map convenience property rebuilt the same axis-name binding as a fresh dict plus MappingProxyType on every access. Earlier Tensor gardening had removed internal dependency on this mapping view, leaving a redundant parallel representation on the contained experimental line.
primary_claim: TensorView now exposes its canonical axes tuple as the single retained axis representation and no longer exposes the redundant axis_map mapping view. Axis ordering, labels, shape, sparse selection/indexing, wire serialization, digest identity, Fourfold/Forest source binding, status and provenance semantics remain unchanged.
gardener_decision: Delete the dead derived axis mapping view before the experimental Tensor surface can harden into another compatibility contract. Reuse the already canonical TensorView.axes tuple rather than retain or cache a second axis-name representation; do not add a lookup service, cache, alternate Tensor type, planner, store, registry, scheduler or backend.
acceptance: the canonical axes tuple remains named, sorted and directly iterable as the single axis representation
